subject: Compact leadership briefing & QBR cascade plan
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Mar 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Compact leadership briefing & QBR cascade plan

Team —

As we prep the April QBR I wanted to circulate a very tight leadership briefing that we can cascade to squads next week. The ask is small: please review the proposed role coverage adjustments and the abridged OKR mapping in the attached matrix and reply with any redlines by EOD tomorrow. I want to lock messaging before the exec readout on Friday so we have consistent talking points for managers.

High-level intent: compress cross-pillar ownership on two fast-impact areas (inference economics + reliability) and avoid a large round of role moves ahead of Q2. This is a focused coverage shift (0.5 FTE equivalents in a few spots) — not a broad reorg. Intended benefits: clearer escalation paths during QBR, concentrated ownership for cost/perf initiatives, and a simpler on-call handoff for the next six weeks.

Attachments: compact_role_matrix_v1.xlsx (proposed splits & owners)

Specific asks:
- Laura: quick read for comm tone and any sensitive phrasing we should avoid for ICs
- Marissa: confirm the impact on Platform OKRs and whether any milestones shift
- Jonas: FYI and approval to cascade once Laura/Marissa sign off

I'm also including a short draft of the manager-facing email at the bottom of the matrix — please flag any phrasing that elevates uncertainty.

Thanks —
Jordan
Jordan Blake
VP, Product Strategy
Redwood Inference

--

Subject: Re: Compact leadership briefing & QBR cascade plan

Jordan —

Thanks for the crisp framing. I scanned the matrix and added inline notes (see redline_notes.docx). A couple of quick items I want us to tighten before we send to managers:

1) Tone: avoid words like "reassign" or "replace" — prefer "short-term coverage" and "temporary stewardship".
2) Communications: managers will need a one-pager FAQ for ICs on compensation/raises and reporting lines. Recommend we add a single FAQ slide to the Drive folder.
3) Stakeholders to loop: Legal should get sight-of the final messaging (simple FYI) and Recruiting for backfill planning in case we convert coverage to permanent roles.

Minor redlines I made in the matrix: swapped suggested owner for the serving-cache lead (to keep on-call locality), and noted a 2-week overlap window for the handoff.

I'll attach a short manager FAQ draft by EOD.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of People Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks Jordan — quick operational notes from Platform:

- The coverage changes look reasonable but I need to confirm headcount downstream impact. If we shift 0.5 FTE equivalents into the inference-perf lane, that will move two milestone owners on the SLAs timeline; I put an initial snapshot in qbr_okr_snapshot.csv.
- Implication for QBR narrative: we should quantify near-term impact on median latency and token cost; I'll pull 14-day rolling numbers and add to the slide deck.
- Can we avoid external customer mentions in the initial manager email? Natalie at Acme Health is on our advisory call next week and I don't want them to see operational chatter before we brief them.

I looped Tyler for capacity planning notes (cc'ed). I'll aim to have the OKR snapshot and slides by tomorrow midday.

Marissa Cole
Director, Platform
Redwood Inference

All —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the thoughtful redlines. I reviewed Laura's notes and Marissa's snapshot. Approve sending the manager-facing email with the language swaps Laura suggested and the FAQ included. A couple of final operational asks before we cascade:

- Add an explicit two-week overlap in the message (operational handoff window)
- Include a single contact for escalation for the duration (suggest: Marissa on platform issues, Laura for people queries)
- Keep Acme Health and other customers off the initial send list; we brief them after managers have the context.

Jordan — authorize the send once Laura uploads the FAQ and Marissa confirms the metrics slide. If either of those slips, hold the send; we cannot have managers getting questions we can't answer.

Jonas Weber
Chief Operating Officer
Redwood Inference
